gloss: being fed up; being sick and tired (of)

definitions.gloss: being fed up; being sick and tired of
definitions.explanation: The state of being thoroughly bored or fed up with something after too much of it. A reduplicated, emphatic form of {飽|あ}きる (to grow tired of). Most often used as {飽|あ}き{飽|あ}きする.

examples.japanese: この{仕事|しごと}には{飽|あ}き{飽|あ}きした。
examples.english: I'm sick and tired of this job.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}{同|おな}じメニューで{飽|あ}き{飽|あ}きしている。
examples.english: I'm fed up with the same menu every day.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{自慢話|じまんばなし}にはみんな{飽|あ}き{飽|あ}きしているようだ。
examples.english: Everyone seems to be sick and tired of his bragging.

notes:
An emphatic, reduplicated form of {飽|あ}きる expressing strong, exasperated boredom — much stronger than simply being a little bored. Almost always used with する: {飽|あ}き{飽|あ}きする.

USAGE:
- The thing one is fed up with takes に: Xに{飽|あ}き{飽|あ}きする.
- {飽|あ}き{飽|あ}きだ also occurs as a predicate: もう{飽|あ}き{飽|あ}きだ (I've had more than enough).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {飽|あ}きる: to grow tired of — the plain verb, neutral and less emphatic
- うんざり: fed up, disgusted — close in meaning, emphasizing exasperation
